handoff.salientSummary: Round 3 of user testing for guest-channels-and-crm: both orchestrator-named assertions pass on commit d8b41f4e. VAL-ONLINE-002's ETag clause holds (fresh date 0 -> new ETag after the first booking; 304 replay before, 200 + new ETag after). VAL-CROSS-007 passes all 5 steps, including the warmed-cache Sites reload that failed in round 2. All 181 in-scope assertions are now passed; services stopped and fixtures restored.
handoff.whatWasImplemented: Ran user-testing validation round 3 for milestone guest-channels-and-crm. Scope was exactly the two assertions named by the orchestrator: VAL-CROSS-007 end to end (including the Sites time chips after a warmed-cache reload) and the ETag clause of VAL-ONLINE-002. Setup: started tenant-api-us (3007), App (3001, VITE_DIRECT_DEV=1) and Sites (3008) via services.yaml, verified all healthchecks and that all acme reservations flags are true, cleared rsv_rate_counters (test-env reset with round-2 precedent), and pre-verified two fresh never-mutated dates (2026-11-29, 2026-12-03 both dayVersion 0 / ETag "0.68.11"). Wrote a round-3 guidance block into library/user-testing.md (scope, fix description, environment state, data-isolation registry, serial rules, per-surface guidance, concurrency plan). Spawned two flow-validator subagents in serial batches (A: r3-etag-api curl-only on 2026-11-29; B: r3-cross007 agent-browser App+Sites plus curl on 2026-12-03) because the browser group's pacing/service-availability writes bump every bookable date's day version and would have invalidated batch A's cached ETag mid-test. Synthesized the results, preserved the round-2 synthesis as synthesis-round2.json, updated validation-state.json (VAL-CROSS-007 failed -> passed, its stale round-2 issue record removed), appended the round-3 results/runtime findings to user-testing.md, and tore the services down.

tests.coverage: No test files were added (validation-only feature). Coverage: VAL-ONLINE-002's ETag clause verified end to end via curl on a never-mutated date (304 replay, first-write version bump, 200 + new ETag after a hold+booking, sqlite proof); VAL-CROSS-007 verified across all five journey steps on a fresh date through the real surfaces (App Settings + Book sheet in agent-browser, Sites /reserve in agent-browser with a warmed-cache plain reload, tenant-api curl for public/operator availability and staff bookings, read-only sqlite for state), plus a full fixture restore and a parent re-check that both channels returned to baseline.

discoveredIssues.description: In this browser session agent-browser's Chrome never revalidated its cached availability body (no If-None-Match, no 304 on a plain reload), so the warmed-cache check alone cannot distinguish 'the fix works' from 'the browser did not cache'. The round-2 defect path was still proven with a curl replay of the pre-change ETag (now 200 + new body) and a labelled in-page default-cache fetch; the user-visible plain reload also showed the closed note with zero stale chips.
discoveredIssues.suggestedFix: If a future round needs to prove HTTP revalidation from the browser itself, drive it with an in-page fetch that keeps If-None-Match (or curl) rather than relying on Chrome's reload behaviour; the round-3 guidance block records this.

discoveredIssues.description: Known quirks re-confirmed: on a replace day the operator availability read still lists slots for every location service rather than only the day's resolved services; the App booking sheet auto-ticks 'Override slot pacing cap' when a pacing-full slot is selected; operator availability on an online_closed day returns the full slot list with dayState.state 'online_closed' (staff unaffected), while 0 slots is the closed day's value.
discoveredIssues.suggestedFix: Optional polish only - none of these contradict the validation contract; the sheet's '*' marker and pacing alert now appear, so the round-2 UI deviation is gone.

deviations.whatIDidInstead: Two flow validators for the two assertions, run in two serial batches (curl group first, browser group second) instead of concurrently.
deviations.why: The browser group's pacing/service-availability writes call bumpBookingHorizonDayVersions, which bumps every bookable date in the horizon and would have invalidated the curl group's cached ETag mid-test.

deviations.whatIDidInstead: Deleted all rows from rsv_rate_counters in the acme tenant DB as a round-start environment reset, and documented it in the round-3 guidance block.
deviations.why: Browser validators cannot set X-Forwarded-For, so they share the durable public buckets (book_ip 20/day, holds_ip 10/10 min); the reset matches the precedent already recorded for round 2 in user-testing.md and touches only ephemeral rate-limit state.

suggestedChanges: For re-run rounds the skill could say explicitly that when the failed assertion's fix changes a setting that bumps shared version counters, the affected groups must be serialized rather than run concurrently - the isolation analysis in Step 3c is where this surfaced here.
